Author: Surya Kant
Bench: Surya Kant
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Original Jurisdiction
 Transfer Petition (Civil) No.2178/2022
 Juhi Poria Petition
 Versus
 Pradip Poria Responde
 O R D E R

1. The petitioner-wife seeks transfer of M.C. No.135/2022, titled Pradip Poria v. Juhi Poria filed by the respondent-husband seeking decree of divorce under Section 13(1)(ia) & (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
The above-stated petition has been filed in the Court of Principal Senior Civil Judge, Bangalore Rural, Bangalore, Karnataka.

entities.text: Court of Principal Senior Civil Judge, Bangalore Rural, Bangalore, Karnataka
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner-wife seeks transfer thereof to the Principal Judge, Family Court, Raipur, Chhattisgarh.
2. The marriage between the parties was solemnized on 29.06.2012 at Durg, Chhattisgarh.
They are blessed with two children, namely, a son born on 11.08.2013 and a daughter born in the year 2018.
Both the children are under the care and custody of the petitioner-wife.

3. While the petitioner-wife is stated to be unemployed, the respondent-husband is working as Senior Customer Service Agent in Singapore Airlines.
4.
It appears that there has been a marital discord 17:38:12 IST between the parties since the year 2014, which eventually led to filing of a complaint by the petitioner-wife in the year 2018.

Thereafter, the respondent-husband has filed the divorce petition, and the petitioner-wife has got FIR No.62/2022 lodged under Sections 498-A and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short, the IPC) against the respondent-husband at Police Station Mahila Thana, Raipur, Chhattisgarh.
5. Since the divorce petition has been filed by the respondent-husband at Bangalore, the petitioner-wife has filed the instant transfer petition seeking transfer on various grounds.
6. With a view to explore the possibility of amicable settlement, the parties were referred to the Supreme Court Mediation Centre.

sentences.text: The parties have now moved a joint application (IA No.260158/2024) invoking powers of this Court under Article 142 of the Constitution of India on the basis of a settlement agreement arrived at between them on 27.07.2024, a copy whereof has been appended with the joint application.
8. Through the settlement, the parties have resolved their matrimonial disputes.
The respondent-husband agreed to pay a sum of Rs.42 lakhs towards full and final permanent alimony to the petitioner-wife.
We are informed that the said agreed amount has been fully paid to the petitioner-wife.
The respondent-husband has further undertaken to pay Rs.2 lakhs every year in the month of April towards the educational expenses of the children till they complete their graduation.
The said amount for the year 2024 is yet to be paid.
The respondent-husband undertakes to pay the said amount within four weeks.

9. Similarly, the respondent-husband has transferred plot bearing No. PHN 158/31 (37) located at Jamgaon, Nawapara, Tehsil Abhanpur, District Raipur, Chhattisgarh, by way of a registered gift deed dated 08.08.2024 in favour of the petitioner-wife, and physical possession, along with original documents, has been handed over to her.
10.
The petitioner-wife has also received her jewellery items, the details of which are given in paragraph 7 of the settlement agreement.
11. The respondent-husband belongs to Schedule Caste community.
His children are also entitled to the certificates of being belonging to the said reserved community.

The respondent-husband has,
therefore, agreed to apply and obtain the Schedule Caste certificates for both the children within six months.
12. The parties are further agreed that the sole custody of the children shall remain with the petitioner-wife.
However, the respondent-husband shall have visitation rights with right to take the children out for vacations once a year and on special occasions like birthdays, etc.
The petitioner-wife has agreed to take necessary steps to build the relationship and strengthen the bonding between the father and the children.
13. The respondent-husband has also undertaken to provide a new two-wheeler to the petitioner-wife by 31.08.2025 for her personal use.
14. Both the parties have further undertaken to withdraw the cases filed against each other.
15. Finally, the parties agreed to part ways and to obtain a decree of divorce by mutual consent.
16. The settlement agreement between the parties is duly signed by them, their counsel, and the learned Mediator.
The joint application is duly supported with their respective affidavits.
Copy of the gift deed has also been placed on record.

17. During the course of hearing, we drew attention of counsel for the parties to the averments made by the respondent-husband in his counter affidavit, which he had filed before the settlement Juhi Poria vs Pradip Poria on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82676190/
2 agreement.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To the said counter affidavit, he has pointed out that the son of the parties, who is specially abled, was admitted to NIMHANS, Bengaluru, which is a leading hospital for treatment of mental disorders.
He has further averred that the entire cost of treatment was borne by him.

18. It is not the case of the parties either in the Settlement Agreement or during the course of hearing that their son has fully recovered from the mental ailment or that he no longer requires any further periodical treatment.
The settlement agreement is silent with regard to the medical assistance, which the parties son may require from time to time.

19. While we are inclined to accept the joint prayer made by the parties in the I.A., such acceptance will be subject to the directions, which we propose to issue for the medical care of the parties son.

The instant transfer petition along with the joint application are, accordingly, disposed of in the following terms:
(i) Having regard to the fact that the parties are living separately for more than five years and they have mutually agreed to dissolve their marriage, their prayer is accepted and the marriage between the parties is hereby dissolved by way of decree of divorce by mutual consent.
(ii) M.C. No.135/2022, titled Pradip Poria v. Juhi Poria, which is a petition under Section 13(1)(ia) & (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and which is pending before the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Bangalore Rural, Bangalore, Karnataka is hereby disposed of as having become infructuous.
(iii) FIR No.62/2022 dated 22.03.2022 registered at Police Station Mahila Thana,
Raipur, Chhattisgarh under Section 498A and 34 of IPC and all the proceedings arising therefrom are hereby quashed.
(iv) The respondent-husband shall abide by the undertaking given by him with regard to payment of a sum of Rs.2 lakhs every year in the month of April towards educational expenses of the children till they attain the age of 21 years and/or graduate, whichever is later.

(v) The petitioner-wife shall submit the details of such expenditure like admission fee, tuition fee, hostel fee, boarding and lodging etc., and it shall be the sole responsibility of the respondent-husband to incur such expenditure for the higher education of the children.
(vi) The respondent-husband shall also abide by the other undertakings, like buying a two-wheeler etc., within the time-line agreed above.

(vii) The petitioner-wife as well as the respondent- Juhi Poria vs Pradip Poria on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82676190/
3 husband are directed to take their son Master Prajwal Poria to NIMHANS, Bengaluru, periodically,
strictly as per the medical advice.
In this regard, they will take the child during the coming winter break of 2024.

The respondent-husband is directed to make necessary arrangements for the temporary lodging and travelling expenses for both the children and their mother, namely, the petitioner, as the petitioner-wife will not be in a position to leave the six years old daughter all alone while taking the son for treatment to Bengaluru.

Whether Master Prajwal Poria would require indoor or outdoor treatment, or how many times he is required to visit the hospital, will be left to the wisdom of the doctors and the parties shall strictly follow the medical advice and protocol to ensure proper treatment of Master Prajwal Poria.
